note: Narration catalogue from the game package (section 5). Cue times are aligned to pauses in each recording.

cues.text: Before you lies the water, dark and wide, and far off, almost imagined, an island.
You have stood on this shore before. Every life has a moment like this.
The noise behind you, the unknown ahead, and the quiet question underneath it all.
The old transcripts describe the beginning of the mind as the untaught seeker. The beginner's mind.
Reaching, reaching, and again reaching. You do not need to know what the island holds. You do not need to be ready.
You only need to begin. Take one slow breath. Feel the ground under your feet, and then let it go.
The water is waiting.
You are in the water now, and it is holding you. Do not fight it. The deep mind is not crossed by force.
It is crossed the way you cross any water in the dark, one gentle movement at a time, trusting what you cannot see.
As you swim, things may float up toward you. A memory. A feeling you thought you had finished with.
Do not chase them, and do not push them away. Let them drift past like leaves on a current.
The transcripts say that beneath the surface of every mind there is a sea, and that everything you have ever been is still down there, shining quietly.
Each stroke is a small act of trust. The island is closer than it looks. Keep going.
The island rises out of the water to meet you. Step onto the sand. Stand still for a moment.
Notice how the noise of the outer world grows thinner here, the way mist thins in morning light.
Inland, seven shapes are waiting. Seven doors, each one a mirror for a different part of your own mind.
You do not need to understand them yet. You do not need to open them in any order. Walk slowly.
The island will show you whatever you are ready to see. There is no test here. There is nothing to win.
There is only the quiet work of looking inward, and the strange, gentle joy of being looked back at.
Begin whenever you are ready.
Before you stands the first figure, one arm raised toward the sky, one hand pointing down toward the earth.
Between the two, a current of light. This is the Magician.
In the old Ra contact he is called the Matrix of the Mind, and he is described as the untaught seeker.
The beginner's mind. Reaching, reaching, and again reaching. All magic begins as desire.
Before anything is built, before anything is understood, something in you reaches.
Stand here a while, and ask yourself the oldest question in the world. What am I truly reaching for?
Do not answer quickly. Hold the question lightly, the way you would hold a bird.
It will tell you when it trusts you.
Between two pillars sits a still figure, half hidden behind a veil, with a book of quiet wisdom resting in her lap.
This is the High Priestess.
The Ra contact calls her the Potentiator of the Mind, that which receives your desire and enables it, by reflection and by blessing.
She does not strive. She does not hurry.
She waits, the way deep water waits, and everything you bring to her comes back clearer.
The deepest answers do not arrive when you chase them.
They rise on their own, in silence, the way stars appear when you stop looking directly at them.
Sit with her a while. Rest your question in the quiet. And notice, without forcing it, what begins to surface.
A garden grows here where nothing was planted.
Vines of light climb through the air, and everything is soft, fertile, and unafraid. This is the Empress.
She is what the Ra contact calls the Catalyst of the Mind, that which acts upon the conscious mind to change it.
Life itself is the teacher at this station. Not books, not doctrines. The things that happen to you.
The people who arrive uninvited. The losses that rearranged the furniture of your soul.
Think of what has been changing you lately, without asking your permission. Catalyst is not punishment.
It is the universe knocking on the door, patiently, until you open it. What is it trying to give you?
A throne of dark stone stands on a square of pale light. It is empty, and it is waiting for you.
This is the Emperor.
The Ra contact calls him the Experience of the Mind, and says that the conscious mind is ennobled by the use of the vast resources of the unconscious.
Everything you have lived through is stored here. Not as a burden. As a treasury.
Every hard winter you survived, every small courage nobody saw, every time you began again.
Sit, if only in your imagination, on the throne of your own experience.
Let your life sit beside you like an honored elder. Ask it: what have you made of me?
And listen, the way you would listen to someone you respect.
An archway of three stones, and beneath it a teacher with no face. Only a listening stillness.
This is the Hierophant.
In the Ra contact he is the Significator of the Mind, the meaning your mind has made of everything it has touched.
Ra says the heart of the mind is a dynamic entity which absorbs, and seeks, and attempts to learn. That is you.
Not the thoughts that pass through, but the one who watches them gather.
Stand under the arch and notice the shape of your own inner teacher. It does not lecture. It does not scold.
It simply keeps asking, with infinite patience: what did you learn? Let the question hang in the air like incense.
You do not have to answer it today.
Two paths cross here beneath a bright star, and where they meet, a garden of two trees grows from a single root.
These are the Lovers. The Ra contact calls this the Transformation of the Mind.
The old transcripts speak of two equal choices, neither greater than the other, and the sacred weight of choosing.
Every transformation begins this way. Not with an answer, but with a crossroads.
To become something new, something old must be released, and the choice is always yours.
You do not have to choose now. Only stand at the crossing. Feel the two paths pulling gently, like two hands.
And ask yourself: if I were free, truly free, which way would my heart lean?
A vessel of pure light waits at the edge of a long, straight road that runs to the horizon and beyond it.
This is the Chariot.
Ra calls it the Great Way of the Mind, a reflection and a summary of all six stations you have walked.
Look back for a moment. The reaching of the Magician. The stillness of the Priestess.
The wild garden of the Empress. The throne of the Emperor. The archway of the Hierophant.
The crossroads of the Lovers. They were never separate places.
They were always one road, and you were always walking it. Step into the vessel when you are ready.
The way forward is the way inward, and it has been waiting for you all along.
Turn back toward the water. The island grows smaller behind you, but nothing you found here stays behind.
You came across this water seeking something. You are crossing back as someone.
That is the whole of it, and it is enough. The star you followed here goes with you now.
It was never on the island. It was never in the sky.
It was the light you were carrying the entire time, and the journey only taught you how to see it. Swim gently.
The shore you left is still there, and the noise is still there, but you will not stand on it the same way again.
Go in peace, and remember the way back. The water will always be here.
Give me the next few minutes.
Imagine a house with three rooms.
In the first room, a lamp is lit. That is the mind.
In the second, a fire is burning. That is the body.
In the third there is only darkness, and somewhere in the darkness, a star. That is the spirit.
There are twenty two stations along the way through these rooms.
They are not places on a map. They are moments every human being passes through, in every life, in every day.
Walk with me.
We begin in the first room, where a figure stands before a table of untouched tools, a bright and empty sky above his head.
This is the Magician. Consciousness itself, awake before anything has happened, the open ground on which everything will be built.
Every thought you will ever think begins here, in the bright moment before the thinking starts.
You are standing in it right now.
Behind him, half hidden between two pillars, sits a still and silent figure.
This is the High Priestess. The deep mind beneath the busy mind, the still water under the waves.
Everything you have ever known without knowing how you know it lives here.
She asks only one thing. Be quiet enough, and still enough, to hear her.
Then the door opens, and life walks in.
This is the Empress. Everything that happens to you. The surprise. The friction. The delight. The wound.
She does not judge what arrives. She receives it the way the earth receives seed.
Every catalyst is her gift, even the ones that hurt.
What you live through, if you truly digest it, becomes a throne you can sit on.
This is the Emperor. Your hard won understanding. The steady authority of someone who walked through fire and kept the warmth.
Feel the weight of everything you have survived. It is holding you up.
And then someone new appears. Someone who can direct all of this.
This is the Hierophant. The will. The chooser. The part of you that decides what your knowing is for.
Until now, life has mostly been happening to you.
From here, you begin to happen to life.
But every real change of mind passes through a single gate.
This is the Lovers. Not romance. The great sorting of the heart.
Will you radiate outward, giving. Or draw inward, gathering.
There is no wrong answer here, only a true one. Feel which way you lean.
That leaning is already transforming you.
And now, everything harnessed at once. Consciousness. Depth. Catalyst. Experience. Will. Love.
This is the Chariot. Not arrival, but direction.
The whole mind moving as one thing.
Feel that forward pull. That is what a clear mind feels like.
The first room is walked. Follow me down the stairs, into the room where the fire is burning.
The body does not begin with thought. It begins with breath. With pulse. With reaching.
This is Strength. Not force. The old, balanced knowing of the animal you are.
Put your hand on your chest.
That rhythm never asked your permission, and it never failed you.
But the fire needs tending, and for that you need a lantern.
This is the Hermit. The quiet counsel that knows when to act and when to rest, what to take in and what to refuse.
He does not shout.
In the noise of every day, his is the smallest voice, and the truest.
Then the wheel turns, and other people walk into your life.
This is the Wheel of Fortune. Every encounter offers something. Wanted or unwelcome. Pleasant or painful.
Each person is an invitation. Each friction, a question addressed to you personally.
Watch what the wheel brings you this week.
What you do with those invitations becomes your harvest.
This is Justice. Not punishment. Not reward. The way a field returns exactly what was planted.
Every kindness you ever planted is growing somewhere.
Look at your life like a field, and you will see what you have been growing.
And here the road asks something difficult.
This is the Hanged Man. The willing surrender. The body offered, turned upside down, given freely so that love might be learned.
Sometimes growth does not look like climbing.
Sometimes it looks like letting go, and trusting.
What you release does not vanish. It transforms.
This is Death. Not an ending. The body's native rhythm.
Every night a small dying. Every morning a small rebirth.
You have died a thousand times already. And here you are.
And all of it, slowly, blends.
This is Temperance. The long alchemy. Everything gathered, poured into one vessel, mixed over a lifetime.
Not a single decisive act. A patient, daily pouring.
This is the great way of the body. To become, gradually and wholly, yourself.
Two rooms walked. Now the stairs go down further, past where the light reaches.
Do not fear this room. The darkness here is not evil. It is simply unlit.
This is the Devil, the matrix of the spirit. Everything in you that you have never looked at directly.
It is not here to punish you.
It waits the way a dark field waits for morning. To be seen.
And sometimes the seeing comes all at once, like lightning.
This is the Tower. A flash in which something you built your life on is revealed as hollow.
It is terrifying. It is also mercy.
What falls was never holding you up.
After the lightning, a star. Small. Distant. Steady.
This is the Star. The bare willingness to keep walking toward a light you cannot prove is there.
You do not need to see the destination.
You only need to not stop.
But the road between the star and the dawn is lit only by the moon.
This is the Moon. Partial seeing. Shapes without names.
Beautiful things and treacherous things look alike in moonlight.
Humility is the only lantern that works in this stretch.
And then, morning.
This is the Sun. The spirit grown past seeking, into radiating.
You no longer chase the light. You have become a source of it.
This is maturity. Not perfection. Radiance.
One day the spirit looks back over everything it has been.
This is Judgement. The great hearing.
What is finite simply falls away, the way a coat falls from shoulders that no longer need it.
You were never the coat.
And at last, the dance.
This is the World. Every station you have walked, mind and body and spirit, gathered into a single turning figure.
Contact with the infinite. Joy without a reason. Not an ending. A wholeness.
You contain the whole road now. And the road contains you.
Twenty one stations behind you. One remains.
At a cliff's edge stands a traveler with empty hands and a full heart.
This is the Fool. The Choice.
In a single moment, the direction of a life is set. Radiance or contraction. Giving or gathering.
The cliff is not a danger. It is an invitation.
And the step is yours.
So here we are, at the end of the road and also at its beginning.
Twenty two stations, and every one of them is inside you at this very moment.
The mind's lamp. The body's fire. The spirit's star.
The only question left is the one the traveler is asking.
Which way will you step.
